sector_model: Insurance (specialty P&C): premiums, combined ratio, reserves, book value and investment income; OCF is not free cash flow. Pending cash acquisition, so the price is set by the deal terms, not by fundamentals.
thesis: Bowhead Specialty Holdings (NYSE: BOW) is being acquired for cash by American Family Mutual Insurance Company, S.I. (merger agreement dated 2026-08-02, announced 08-03; about 1.2B). 8-K 2026-11-13 (read in full): stockholders approved the merger at the 11-13 special meeting, 80.60% of outstanding shares for (77.33% excluding parent and recused directors); closing remains subject to the agreement's other conditions (regulatory approvals per news coverage; not listed in the 8-K). Deal price 34.00 per share in cash, about 11% over the 07-31 unaffected 30.59 close; the 34.00 comes from search summaries of news and the deal press release (not read directly). Close 11-17 is 34.17 (34.12 on 11-16, 34.13 on 11-13), 0.5% above 34.00, so the market is pricing near-certain completion and a possible small dividend or other value, which is unexplained here. Q3 2026 (release read): gross written premium 256.4M (+10.8%), net earned premium 150.2M (+17.0%), net income 12.9M, combined ratio 95.9%; 9M NI 45.1M, combined ratio 95.7%; BVPS 13.75, equity 451.1M, debt 146.7M, reserves 1,432.4M, investments 1,622.9M. TTM NI 59.9M; market cap about 1126M (32,945,158 shares at the 10-12 record date) = 18.8x TTM NI, 2.50x book. The upside is capped near the offer; this is a merger-arbitrage situation, not a fundamental value idea, and a fresh buyer earns about the spread (negative) unless a higher bid emerges.
counterthesis: At 34.17 against a 34.00 cash offer there is no positive spread to capture and downside if the deal breaks (unaffected price 30.59, about 10% lower, or lower if regulators or reserves intervene). Going-private deals with an existing 14.3% holder carry conflict risk; eleven demand letters and two complaints seek to enjoin it. CFO Mulcahey announced departure in April 2027. Valuation at 2.5x book and 18.8x TTM NI reflects the buyer's premium, not an organic discount. Reserve adequacy for casualty lines (reserves 1,432M against equity 451M) was not examined.
invalidation: The watch view changes if regulators block or delay the deal beyond year-end, if an injunction is granted, if a competing bid appears (upside), or if reserve charges alter the buyer's willingness to close.
